hook: An empty hospital room full of things to find: tap each object in the picture, then give it its article.
intro: A picture hunt instead of a deck: one empty hospital room, the kind you see when you visit someone on a ward, with 32 things to find in it, every one a precise noun you rarely meet in a textbook — der Bettgalgen over the bed, die Schnabeltasse on the bedside cabinet, das Röntgenbild on the wall, der Treteimer by the basin. The prompt asks Wo ist …? and you tap the object in the picture. Each find shows its label, coloured by its gender, then leaves a small tick in that colour, so you can see what you have already found. A tap on bare wall costs nothing; a tap on the wrong object tells you what you hit and you keep looking, and after three misses the right one is shown. Once you have passed a run, the hunt turns harder: the prompt hides the article (Wo ist ___ Schnabeltasse?), and after the find you choose der, die or das yourself. No object is asked twice in the same run.
tips[0].title: Compounds in the hospital room: the last part decides
tips[0].text: Hospital words are long, but only the last part decides the article. Sauerstoff + Flasche: die Flasche, so die Sauerstoffflasche. Infusion + Ständer: der Ständer, so der Infusionsständer. Ignore the front; read the end.
tips[0].check.why: The last part is der Spender, so the whole word is der Desinfektionsmittelspender.
tips[1].title: Same last part, same article — even when it looks odd
tips[1].text: die Wärmflasche is a rubber bag, not a bottle at all, but it ends in die Flasche, so it is feminine. das Kopfkissen and das Klemmbrett follow das Kissen and das Brett. Trust the last word, not what the object looks like.
tips[1].check.why: The last part is die Tasse, so it is die Schnabeltasse.
tips[2].title: Things that hold something: der Beutel, der Eimer, der Ständer
tips[2].text: Many containers and holders in this room are masculine: der Infusionsbeutel, der Treteimer, der Infusionsständer, der Nachttisch. Picture a nurse, Herr Beutel, carrying all of them past the bed; say each one with der as he passes.
tips[2].check.why: The last part is der Tisch, so it is der Nachttisch.
remember[0]: The last part of a compound sets the article: die Flasche → die Sauerstoffflasche, die Wärmflasche.
remember[1]: das Bett, das Kissen, das Brett stay neuter inside compounds: das Krankenbett, das Kopfkissen, das Klemmbrett.
remember[2]: Loanwords often keep a fixed gender to learn by heart: der Paravent, das Stethoskop, das Rollo.
